qt: to the Commission Anna Maria Cisint (PfE) Subject:

Recent cyber-attacks against critical infrastructure and services highlight Member States’ vulnerability to threats liable to compromise the security and operational continuity of strategic sectors. European defence cannot be circumscrlimited to the military sphere; it must also encompass the protection of schools, hospitals, power grids, ports, railway terminals, logistics hubs, businesses and digital infrastructure. One key concern relates to external suppliers authorised to access the IT and operational systems of such infrastructure: unmonitored access could represent vulnerabilities that could be exploited for infiltration, sabotage and cyber-attacks. While the NIS2 Directive sets out requirements regarding security of supply chains and oversight of access to IT systems, compliance with them needs to be ensured, particularly in dealings with external suppliers of strategic European infrastructure. In the light of the above: 1.
What measures does the Commission intend to take so as to better protect schools and European critical infrastructure, particularly in the transport, health-care, energy, rail and IT sectors?

Does the Commission have any data on the effectiveness of the measures provided for in the NIS2 Directive in preventing unauthorised access and leaks of sensitive data via external suppliers, and how do the legislative initiatives presented in January 2026 aim to strengthen these safeguards?
